name: Bench
description: A single-file H5 workshop planner. A production plan is two quantities, and every other number on screen — what each raw part is needed in, what is short, what putting it right costs, how many more you could make — comes from exploding a bill of materials down through a shared sub-assembly and netting it against the shelf. Two things stop it being mental arithmetic: the six ready-built leg assemblies run out partway through, so the rest have to be made from raw stock, which pulls in screws the products were also counting on; and nothing is sold singly, so being two dowels short and being twenty-five short cost exactly the same £15. 5 screens, an expandable parts tree, a shelf with pack sizes, and a purchase basket.

finish.answer: final answer for question tasks; optional for action tasks

observation.text: engine.a11y(state) — the parts tree serialises with its indentation, quantities and per-unit multipliers, and every shelf line prints stock, requirement and shortfall, so the whole explosion is checkable without pixels.
observation.pixels: 390x844 screenshot (browser backend); __ENV__.bounds() maps every test-id to a pixel box
observation.state: engine.snapshot(state) — canonical state plus a derived view keyed by part name. For the verifier only.

world.bom: bench = 2 seat planks + 4 leg assemblies + 12 screws; side table = 1 top + 4 leg assemblies + 8 screws; leg assembly = 1 square stock + 2 dowels + 4 screws
world.stock: 20 seat planks, 3 tops, 30 square stock, 50 dowels, 200 screws, and 6 leg assemblies already built
world.packs: seat planks 5 at £120, tops 1 at £86, square stock 10 at £90, dowels 25 at £15, screws 100 at £24
world.seeded: 6 benches and 3 side tables — 10 dowels and 16 screws short, £39.00 to put right
world.frontier: with nothing bought the shelf carries (7,0), (6,1), (5,2) or (4,3); one bench per table, all the way down
world.contention: the plan needs 216 screws but the products only ask for 96 — the other 120 go into the 30 legs that have to be built
world.cliff: £40 of parts reaches 9 benches; £100 reaches no further, because the next part to run out only comes ten to a pack at £90
